$comment: Fault code to service-route table. This is the spine of the portal. Because every leg returns to ERS anyway, most faults do not need a truck - they need a flag on the leg's record that diverts it at inspection. Only a leg that cannot finish its session earns a dispatch.

self.label: Operator-serviceable
self.action: Follow the linked procedure. No ticket, no record change.

flag.label: Flag for ERS
flag.action: The leg finishes its session and is diverted at ERS inspection when it returns. No truck is sent.

dispatch.label: Dispatch replacement
dispatch.action: The leg cannot finish its session. A healthy leg is sent from the pool and the failed leg returns to check-in.

subsystems.PWR: Power — 56 V motor bus and 24 V logic
subsystems.DRV: Drive axis — ClearPath-SC servo and driven caster
subsystems.LFT: Lift axis — ClearPath-SC servo and lift column

codes.title: Pack charge below session reserve
codes.meaning: Remaining charge will not cover the declared session plus the return transit.
codes.remedy: Swap the pack at the facility bank before claiming the leg. Charge state is never a field repair — legs do not charge on the belt.

codes.title: 56 V bus fault
codes.meaning: Motor bus out of tolerance. The ClearCore inhibits both axes.
codes.remedy: Do not bypass the pack interlock. The leg cannot take load and cannot walk itself to transport.

codes.title: 24 V logic rail unstable
codes.meaning: Logic supply is browning out under motor load.
codes.remedy: The leg may appear healthy at rest and drop mid-lift. Take it out of the session now.

codes.title: Driven caster slip
codes.meaning: Commanded and measured travel disagree on the driven caster.
codes.remedy: Usually debris or a wet floor on the approach lane. Clear the lane and re-run convergence.

codes.title: Drive servo current trending high
codes.meaning: ClearPath-SC drawing above its envelope for the commanded travel over the last 20 sessions.
codes.remedy: Early gearbox wear. The leg is safe to finish its session; wear accrues against the mechanical serial.

codes.title: Drive axis stalled
codes.meaning: The driven caster will not turn under command.
codes.remedy: The leg cannot converge, cannot self-load, and cannot walk off. It must be carried out.

codes.title: Lift height disagreement
codes.meaning: One leg in the module reports 4-10 mm off the module's commanded height.
codes.remedy: Re-run module levelling. If it returns within ten cycles, raise it to a flag.

codes.title: Lift holding drift
codes.meaning: The column lost more than 6 mm over a 30-minute static hold.
codes.remedy: Safe below 80% rated module load. Do not assign this leg to a walk-off until it has been through the line.

codes.title: Lift axis will not hold
codes.meaning: The column drops under load or will not reach commanded height.
codes.remedy: Set the structure down on its own supports before releasing anyone into the work area.

codes.title: Over-travel on lift column
codes.meaning: The column exceeded its mechanical stroke limit.
codes.remedy: Assume column and end-stop damage. The leg is exchanged, never adjusted on site.

codes.title: Firmware behind fleet
codes.meaning: This leg is running a version older than the fleet's stable channel.
codes.remedy: The session controller pushes the bundle on the next dock. No action unless it persists across two returns.

codes.title: ClearCore fault
codes.meaning: The controller failed self-test and will not command either axis.
codes.remedy: Not field-repairable. Note the electronics serial — the replacement carries a different one and the fleet record rolls over.

codes.title: XBee link marginal
codes.meaning: Packet loss to the session controller above threshold, still inside recovery.
codes.remedy: Check the 300 m budget and line of sight. Move the session controller before touching the leg.

codes.title: Leg lost from session
codes.meaning: The session controller stopped hearing a claimed leg entirely.
codes.remedy: Motion inhibits across the whole module by design. Never attempt a manual override on a leg that is out of session.

codes.title: Uplink unavailable
codes.meaning: The session controller cannot reach this portal. Local operation is unaffected.
codes.remedy: Sessions run offline. Firmware and fleet sync resume automatically when the uplink returns.

codes.title: Bracket torque out of spec
codes.meaning: A bracket fastener reported below the seating window at dock.
codes.remedy: Re-seat and re-torque to spec. Attachment is a lookup, not a measurement — never shim the bracket to close a gap.

codes.title: Bracket will not seat
codes.meaning: The leg cannot achieve a valid attachment at its assigned rail point.
codes.remedy: Check the rail point for damage before blaming the leg. If the rail is sound, the bracket face is out and the leg is exchanged.

codes.title: Module pairing refused
codes.meaning: Two legs would not pair — usually a variant or firmware mismatch.
codes.remedy: Pairing is arbitrary. Release both and claim a different pair rather than forcing this one.

codes.title: Service interval reached
codes.meaning: Motor-hours against the mechanical serial crossed the interval, or twelve months elapsed since the last closed service record.
codes.remedy: Flag it. The code clears when ERS closes the service record against the mechanical serial.

codes.title: Leg reported lost across facilities
codes.meaning: The central registry holds no recent check-in for a leg another facility believes it has.
codes.remedy: Do not claim the leg into a session. Report it — the registry exists to stop exactly this becoming a false loss.
